newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan plays down expulsion of ships at islands.
newsitem.headline: Japan plays down expulsion of ships at islands.

text.p: The Japanese coast guard on Monday played down reports that its patrol boats had expelled five boats carrying Taiwan and Hong Kong activists from waters around a chain of disputed East China Sea islands.
"It is our routine duty to issue warnings and ask foreign ships to move out of Japan's territorial waters," said a spokesman for the Maritime Safety Agency on Japan's southernmost island of Okinawa.
"There is no change in our response (to foreign ships)," he told Reuters by telephone.

Earlier on Monday, Taiwan radio reported that Japanese patrol ships had repulsed the boats, which were trying to land Taiwan and Hong Kong activists on a chain of disputed East China Sea islands to defy Tokyo's claim to sovereignty.
"Two of the ships tried to force their way at full speed to the Diaoyu islands but were stopped by Japanese police vessels about 200 metres (yards) away," the radio broadcast said.
"The atmosphere was very tense...They are returning to Taiwan now because the Japanese force is really big," the broadcast said. Japan used 17 coast guard and police ships, it added.
The Japanese coast guard spokesman did not fully confirm the Taiwan radio report but said Japanese patrol boats demanded "some" ships from Taiwan and Hong Kong stay away from the territorial waters.

The five vessels, carring about 20 activists from Taiwan and Hong Kong and up to 60 journalists, set sail on Sunday aiming to challenge Japan's claim of sovereignty to the uninhabited islands, which it calls the Senkakus.
A makeshift lighthouse built on one of the islands in July by a Japanese right-wing group has rekindled a festering dispute over the islands, claimed by Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei.
The Taiwan activists hoped to plant the flag of the island's exiled Republic of China. The Hong Kong protesters were carrying that of the mainland's People's Republic of China.
Apart from the ships warded off on Monday, at least 13 Taiwanese ships have unsuccessfully tried to approach the disputed islands this month, the Japanese coastguard spokesman said.
"There has been no trouble or conflict," he said.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
The Taiwan government also claims ownership of the islands, saying they are under the jurisdiction of the northeastern Taiwanese county of Ilan.
Japan was given control of the islands in 1972 by the United States, which had administered the islands along with Okinawa since the end of World War Two.
